title: R1-B Architecture Recovery
human_intent: Recover PROMETEO LAB R1-B from durable evidence, determine what later Prometeo actually adopted, preserve current technical invariants and negative knowledge, and make continuation possible without old chats or a duplicate architecture.
already_decided: Route to existing Current/Catalog/Lineage/runtime owners before creating architecture.
Candidate, Current, Human Accepted and Served are distinct states and are never promoted by recovery inference.
Context Foundry v1 was explicitly incomplete; Part 2 materialized Context Foundry v2 as a tested candidate and integrated it into the Part 2 platform candidate.
Context Foundry v2 preserves EXISTS != PARTICIPATES, privacy lineage, fail-closed high-authority contradiction handling, deterministic selection and reopen/consumption evidence.
Browser persistence v1.1 uses staged CAS writes, schema/versioned envelopes and migrations; its in-memory/session receipts are diagnostics, not the durable authority ledger.
Part 2 introduced the durable hash-chained receipt ledger, Current/Lineage/continuity/context/workflow/reincarnation composition and tested them as candidate architecture.
Classes runtime v2 and Student World runtime v2 are tested candidates; recovery does not promote them over product-specific owners without later browser/product evidence.
Later P3 release evidence establishes an actual Served release plus canary/rollback/export proof, but does not imply every internal candidate module became Human Accepted or Current in its own scope.
The authority map continues to name runtime-v22 as the champion/reference for persistence and release mechanisms; reuse that evidence rather than inventing a second release stack.
The historical claim that an R1-B package contained 74 files is not treated as durable fact unless exact source bytes/manifest are recovered.
high_value_targets: Leave one durable adoption matrix showing which R1-B ideas survived as current owners, tested candidates, historical references or unresolved evidence.
Prevent future agents from recreating Context Foundry, persistence, release/rollback or authority machinery under new names.
Preserve fail-closed privacy/authority/currentness rules and release truth ceilings.
Separate historical R1-B intent from later verified implementation and serving evidence.
Make future R1-B-adjacent work route directly to the correct owner/path without old chats.
known_failures: Treating a large historical architecture packet as authority merely because a chat claimed it existed.
Assuming the highest version number is the current or Human Accepted implementation.
Treating a candidate commit, a test PASS or a Served visible release as proof that every internal module is Human Accepted.
Building another Context Foundry or memory architecture instead of using the existing source/curation/authority/privacy/working-set layers.
Letting explicit context IDs bypass privacy or letting derived context weaken source privacy.
Selecting superseded historical truth into a current working set by default.
Allowing high-authority contradictions to resolve silently instead of failing closed.
Treating session persistence receipts as the durable authority ledger.
Using a build string alone as semantic restore/catalog compatibility evidence.
Making architecture improvements that regress accepted visible or interaction behavior.
Rewriting PageKit, Classes, Student World, Navigator or product UI just to make the architecture look uniform.
Using source existence or semantic similarity as proof that a source participates in current authority.
do_not_touch: lineage authority or Human Accepted scopes
execution_frontier: Recovery is complete. Consume RECOVERY_2026-09-09 + LAST_RETURN + D-014, and reopen only for a concrete owner-specific defect/request or newly recovered exact historical R1-B source bytes.
stop_only_if: The verified adoption/invariant map is durably published and no concrete owner-specific implementation defect remains inside R02.
A future change would require Human Accepted/Current/Served promotion or product-specific human acceptance.
Missing historical R1-B bytes would be the only way to prove a chat-only claim.
